Scientific name: Pseudexostoma brachysoma Chu, 1979. Family: Sisoridae. Size: 153 mm (6") SL. IUCN Red List: Not Evaluated.

Type locality: hill stream running into the Nu River, near Laowo, Yunlong Xian [now Lushi County, Nujiang Prefecture], Yunnan Province, China.

• IUCN Red List: Data Deficient. The species is restricted to a single river basin where it appears to be uncommon; it is unclear whether threats significantly affect it, and the population trend is unknown (IUCN 2023).
Asia: known only from the middle and lower Nujiang (=Salween) basin, China.
Asia: Salween drainage, China. Type locality: hill stream running into the Nu River, near Laowo, Yunlong Xian, Yunnan, China.
Breeding: unreported. There is no breeding report.

Identification: continuous post-labial groove, gill openings not extending onto the venter, heterodont dentition (different types of teeth) in both jaws. The outer teeth are shovel-shaped and sparsely arranged in one or two rows whilst the inner teeth are conical and numerous. The tooth patches are separated in the upper jaw. 16–18 branched pectoral rays.

Dorsal soft rays (total): 5; anal soft rays: 3-4. This species is distinguished from Pseudexostoma yunnanense by: posterior margin of lower lip with 3 notches, the middle one shallower than the lateral ones (vs. same depth); the 2 smaller median lobes of the lower lip longer than the lateral lobes (vs. the same length); pelvic fin i, 3-4 (vs. i, 5); base of adipose fin longer, 36.1-46.0% SL (vs. 28.8-39.8); caudal peduncle more slender, depth 4.2-6.9% SL, 20-33.7% in length of caudal peduncle (vs. 6.4-8.3 and 32.6-42.7); premaxillary tooth band with 16-18 teeth (vs. 18-22), divided into 2 and isolated (vs. partially connected).

It differs from P. longipterus in having a shorter pectoral fin, 24.9-29.8% SL (vs. 30.1-31.3), pelvic fin 16.1-22.9% SL (23.1-24.3), and caudal fin 13.6-17.9% SL (vs. 18-19.6); smaller eyes and a narrower interorbital width, eye diameter 5.8-7.8% HL (vs. 8.2-10), interorbital width 19.7-24.7% HL (vs. 25.5-30.8).

Etymology: the specific name brachysoma comes from brachýs, short, and sõma, body; it was proposed as a subspecies of P. yunnanense with a shorter body.
Acta Zootaxonomica Sinica v. 4 (no. 1), pp78 [English p. 81], Fig. 3.
